Eli: Heads-up 10min sync: creating a 1-page customer playbook for small onboarding bursts (up to ~3k qps). Need it short, ops-friendly, and copy-pasteable. Draft below.

Nora: Great. Keep it to three actions plus a tiny troubleshooting cheat. Customers skim fast.

Eli: Draft v1: (A) Prefill/top-prefix warm cache for top 8 prompts, (B) Enable micro-batching for short (<300 token) calls, (C) Route nonessential calls to a quantized cheap variant.

Jared: Add a minimal SDK snippet and a curl prefill example. Also recommend a staggered warm schedule to avoid a burst on the backend.

Eli: Adding snippets now.

Nora: Snippet (Python):
```python
# client with batching + small TTL cache
client = Redwood("$API_KEY")
client.configure(batching=True, max_batch_size=6, max_latency_ms=25)
client.cache.enable(prefix_ttl_seconds=240)
```

Jared: Warm plan suggestion: 150 warm requests over 6 minutes (one every 2.4s) hitting top prefixes. Keeps KV cache warm without big spikes. Include a node warmup script too.

Eli: Warm node script (customers can run):
```js
// warmup-run.js
const prompts = ['Hello','Status','FAQ'];
async function warm(client){
 for(let i=0;i<150;i++){
  await client.generate({prompt: prompts[i%prompts.length]});
  await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2400));
 }
}
```

Tess: Ops metrics to show customers: model_p50_latency and cache_hit_rate. Suggest thresholds: p50 < 140ms, cache_hit_rate > 0.5. If cache hit < 0.35 advise prompt canonicalization (trim, lowercase) and ensure prefixes match routing keys.

Jared: For immediate mitigation steps if users still see lag: 1) reduce batch latency to 10ms, 2) switch noninteractive endpoints to "cheap-quant-v1", 3) turn on streaming output so UI can render partial tokens.

Eli: Add a tiny curl prefill for field teams to paste (replace ORG_ID and API_KEY):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/prefill \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
 -d '{"org_id":"ORG-77","prompts":["Welcome","Order lookup","Billing FAQ"]}'
```

Nora: Include a one-paragraph expectation note: "Prefill + warmup typically reduces cold-latency within 3-12 minutes. If not, open a support case and include: traceset ID, sample prompts, and observed p50/p95."

Eli: Good. Also adding a 3-line troubleshooting Q&A:
- Low cache hit -> check canonicalization + mismatch of tenant prefixes.
- Streaming jitter -> increase chunk_size to 64 or lower network buffering.
- Cost spike -> reduce batch window and route to quantized variant.
